boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented High Point University traditions spanning Welcome Week, milestone ceremonies, annual celebrations, and campus community events.

cards.title: Derby Day
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide start-of-year celebration
cards.notes: Look for the early-semester Derby Day program and join the campus activities on the Kester International Promenade when they are announced.
cards.short_summary: A campus-wide event that opens the academic year with shared activities.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU describes Derby Day as a campus-wide party that starts the school year; its Promenade programming has included inflatables, climbing walls, food trucks, and water slides.
cards.source_title: The College Tour at High Point University | Full Episode Part 1
cards.access_notes: Check HPU event communications for the current schedule and participation details.

cards.title: Walk Behind the Waterfall
cards.subtitle: Hoffman Amphitheatre, David R. Hayworth Park
cards.notes: During the first week of class, follow Welcome Week guidance for the waterfall walk at Hoffman Amphitheatre and place a hand in the falling water.
cards.short_summary: New students mark their arrival by passing behind a 15-foot waterfall.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU identifies walking behind the 15-foot waterfall at Hoffman Amphitheatre during the first week of class as a tradition symbolizing good luck at HPU.
cards.source_title: The Parents’ Guide to Values-Based Living and Learning at College
cards.access_notes: Participate only when the university schedules or permits the Welcome Week activity.

cards.title: Start at Opening Convocation
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week academic ceremony
cards.notes: Attend the incoming-class ceremony to hear the university welcome and see faculty process in academic regalia before classes begin.
cards.short_summary: The formal Welcome Week ceremony marks the beginning of a student’s academic journey.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU calls Opening Convocation a long-standing tradition that brings faculty and administration together to welcome new students and set the stage for their education.
cards.access_notes: Use the current Welcome Week schedule for location, guest entry, and timing.

cards.entity_name: High Point University Honor Code Signing
cards.title: Sign the Honor Code
cards.subtitle: Opening Convocation tradition
cards.notes: Bring any required materials to the Welcome Week ceremony and take part when the incoming class recites and signs the Honor Code.
cards.short_summary: New students publicly begin their HPU experience with an Honor Code commitment.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU’s Welcome Week guide states that students recite and sign the High Point University Honor Code for the first time during Opening Convocation.
cards.access_notes: This is scheduled as part of Welcome Week; follow directions from university staff.

cards.title: Pass On an HPU Blanket
cards.subtitle: Convocation and commencement ceremony tradition
cards.notes: At the ceremony, choose someone whose support mattered to you and give them the HPU blanket presented to students or graduates.
cards.short_summary: Students receive a blanket intended for a person who helped them reach the milestone.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU says blankets are presented at convocation and graduation for students to give to someone who made a significant impact in their life.
cards.access_notes: Blanket distribution is part of designated university ceremonies; confirm ceremony instructions with HPU.

cards.title: Watch the Commencement Eagle Flight
cards.subtitle: HPU graduation ceremony
cards.notes: From your assigned commencement seating, watch for the university’s ceremonial eagle flight at the end of the program and follow event staff directions.
cards.short_summary: A bald eagle’s flight closes HPU’s graduation ceremony as a ceremonial symbol.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU reports that a bald eagle named Clark traditionally soars over graduates at the end of commencement to symbolize free enterprise, independence, and opportunity.
cards.source_title: High Point University Celebrates Class of 2026 with Former Walmart International CEO
cards.access_notes: Viewing is part of the official commencement program; follow university event and animal-handling instructions.

cards.title: Volunteer at the Veterans Day Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Annual salute to military veterans
cards.notes: Watch for HPU’s Veterans Day registration and volunteer information, then support the annual breakfast honoring military veterans and their service.
cards.short_summary: HPU annually convenes a breakfast and patriotic salute for military heroes.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU’s 2026 Veterans Day Celebration page identifies an annual patriotic salute and breakfast for military heroes.
cards.access_notes: The 2026 celebration is scheduled for November 6; registration and details will be posted by HPU.

cards.title: Find the Halloween Candy Handout
cards.subtitle: President Qubein’s campus walkabout
cards.notes: On Halloween, keep an eye on the Café, sidewalks, and student center for President Qubein’s giant-candy-bar handout and a brief greeting.
cards.short_summary: A Halloween presidential walkabout includes giant candy bars for students.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU states that President Qubein gives giant candy bars to students he sees around the Café, sidewalks, and student center on Halloween.
cards.source_title: A Day in the Life | Undergraduate Admissions
cards.access_notes: Locations and timing can vary; rely on current university announcements and do not block campus walkways.

cards.entity_name: Valentine’s Day Giant Candy Bar Handout
cards.title: Find the Valentine’s Candy Handout
cards.subtitle: President Qubein’s campus walkabout
cards.notes: On Valentine’s Day, look around the Café, sidewalks, and student center for President Qubein’s giant-candy-bar handout and a chance to say hello.
cards.short_summary: The Valentine’s Day counterpart to HPU’s presidential candy-bar tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU states that President Qubein gives giant candy bars to students he sees around the Café, sidewalks, and student center on Valentine’s Day.
cards.source_title: A Day in the Life | Undergraduate Admissions
cards.access_notes: Locations and timing can vary; rely on current university announcements and do not block campus walkways.

cards.title: Close the Year at the Carnival
cards.subtitle: End-of-year student celebration
cards.notes: Check the student-events calendar near the final day of classes and attend the Carnival as a daytime way to mark the end of the academic year.
cards.short_summary: An annual student celebration recognizes the last day of classes.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU’s Traditions & Values program identifies the last day of class Carnival as an annual event for students to celebrate the end of the year.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current date, location, and entry requirements through HPU student-event communications.
